newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom sees ongoing intense competition.
newsitem.headline: Telecom sees ongoing intense competition.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand said on Wednesday it expects competition in New Zealand's telecommunications market to remain intense, with the prospects of existing participants extending their activities and new market entrants.
In 1996 Telecom concluded an interconnection agreement with Telstra New Zealand Ltd enabling Telstra to offer national and international calls and 0800 services.
Clear Communications Ltd has indicated it will offer local call services to customers in the Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch central business districts.
"Telecom anticipates significant competition in these areas and in calls to its cellular network," Telecom said at the release of its annual profit.
"Clear has stated it might also offer local call services to some residential customers. The impact on Telecom's revenues as Clear extends its services cannot be reliably assessed at this time."

Saturn Communications Ltd was also seeking interconnection with Telecom to provide local call services, in addition to the pay television services it plans to roll out in selected areas of Wellington and Auckland.
"Negotiations are under way with BellSouth New Zealand Ltd which provides competing cellular services, on a broader interconnection agreement than the one signed in March 1993," Telecom said.
It said it was currently in negotiation with carriers in respect of number portability, which allows a customer to retain a telephone number when changing carriers.

"Telecom anticipates that the necessary agreements can be reached and that number portability can be implemented this year. The effect, if any, upon Telecom's revenues cannot be measured at this time," Telecom said.
